topics.label: Lecture introduction and aims
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture as an integration of previously introduced immune cells and molecules.

topics.label: Principles of innate immune recognition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how innate immune recognition depends on matching pathogen or damage signals with appropriately positioned, genetically encoded receptors.

topics.label: Toll-like receptors and their signaling
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how toll-like receptors translate microbial recognition into immune responses suited to the location and nature of infection.

topics.label: Non-TLR recognition and inflammasome activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics show how danger-sensing pathways beyond toll-like receptors connect microbial products and cellular damage to inflammation.

topics.label: Sentinel-driven inflammation and leukocyte recruitment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how activated sentinel cells mobilize an inflammatory response that brings circulating immune cells to infected tissue.

topics.label: Lymphatic transport and adaptive immune priming
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how the lymphatic drainage system enables activated dendritic cells to carry evidence of infection to lymph nodes for adaptive immune activation.

topics.label: Excessive inflammation and septic shock
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how an excessive systemic inflammatory response can produce dangerous cardiovascular effects and lasting harm.

topics.label: Mechanisms of inflammation resolution
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how inflammation subsides through the balance between declining inflammatory stimulation and active inhibitory signals.

topics.label: Tissue repair and persistent inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine why the response to damaged tissue sometimes restores homeostasis but sometimes persists as chronic inflammation that can be harmful or protective.

topics.label: Lecture close and next lecture
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic ends the lecture and announces complement as the subject of the next lecture.
